topic: How does the hybrid SIW-waveguide feeding topology balance efficiency and compactness in V-band satellite antenna designs?
consensus_response: The hybrid SIW-waveguide feeding topology achieves a balance between efficiency and compactness by optimizing the transition between SIW and waveguide sections. This is achieved through careful design of the transition stubs, matching networks, and material selection. By minimizing insertion loss and ensuring seamless power transfer, the hybrid topology can provide high-gain, wide-bandwidth, and compact antennas that meet the stringent requirements of V-band satellite communication. This topology may influence future satellite antenna designs by promoting modular, high-efficiency, and adaptable systems.
reference_context: A wideband high-gain high-efficiency hybrid integrated plate array antenna for V-band inter-satellite links is presented, consisting of microstrip patches, substrate integrated waveguide (SIW), and waveguide power dividers. The hybrid SIW-waveguide feeding topology is optimized to realize high efficiency, low cost, and compact configuration. Measured results demonstrate a reflection coefficient bandwidth of 14.6% and a gain of 39.2 dBi at 59 GHz with an efficiency of 41%.
